title: Privilege of Charles V, 23 March 1530, granting the islands of Malta and Gozo and the fortress of Tripoli to the Order of Saint John
exact_locator: The privilege enumerates the islands of Malta and Gozo, held as fiefs of the Kingdom of Sicily, together with the fortress of Tripoli; studied with Latin extracts by Aleksander Cieslak, 'Emperor Charles V's Privilege of 1530 Granting the Malta and Gozo Islands as Well as the Fortress of Tripoli to the Knights Hospitaller', Roczniki Humanistyczne 50/2 (2002)
statement: The grant is a perpetual fief under imperial suzerainty as king of Sicily, against the annual tribute of a falcon; it names Malta and Gozo, and it does not name Comino.
interpretation: The territorial title, and the reason Gozo can be authorised at all: the instrument enumerates it. Comino is absent from the enumeration, so Comino is not authorised from this assertion - the answer comes from what the document says, not from the geography.

title: Establishment of the Order's printing press in the magistral palace by Grand Master Manuel Pinto de Fonseca, opened to the public on 5 June 1756
exact_locator: Government of Malta, Government Printing Press, 'Press History', Development of Printing: Don Nicolo Capaci commissioned by Grand Master Pinto in 1756; the press opened to the public on 5 June 1756 and the first paid commission was printed in July 1756
statement: The sovereign of the islands set up a state press inside his own palace, licensed under the 1746 imprimatur settlement between the Grand Master, the Bishop and the Inquisitor, and it printed legal cases among other work.
interpretation: A dated act of government exercised on the island eight weeks before the snapshot, by the Order and in the Order's own seat.

title: Government record series of the Order of Saint John running across 1756
exact_locator: Archives of the Order of Malta, National Library of Malta: Section 2 Libri Conciliorum, AOM 73-254 (1459-1798); Section 5 Libri Bullarum, AOM 316-633 (1346-1798); Section 10 Statutes and Ordinances, AOM 1649-1712; Section 16 General Visits and Land Surveys, AOM 5278-6382
statement: The Council minutes, the registers of magistral bulls, the statutes and ordinances, and the general visits and land surveys all have series date ranges that contain 1756-08-01.
interpretation: Government actually running, evidenced by its own surviving series. The land surveys matter most here: the Order was administering the ground, not merely garrisoning it.

title: French occupation of the Maltese islands and the end of the Order's rule
exact_locator: Capitulation of the Maltese islands to the French expedition, 12 June 1798; the Order's printer stayed in post 'until the end of the French rule of the Maltese Islands in 1800'
statement: The Order ruled the islands from 1530 until the French took them in 1798.
interpretation: Recorded so that neither the French occupation nor the British protectorate that followed can be back-dated into 1756.
